title: Methodological Constraints & Research Notes
description: Formal constraints, environmental parameters, and analytical boundaries governing the empirical interpretation of this study.

syntheticScope.title: Synthetic Evaluation Scope
syntheticScope.content: Scenarios represent bounded, isolated software-engineering situations designed to evaluate single-step routing choices. They deliberately omit full multi-turn conversational history, developer feedback loops, and live file tree modifications.
syntheticScope.rule: Single-step accuracy does not guarantee end-to-end multi-turn agent task completion.

frozenVsAdaptive.title: Frozen Benchmark vs. Adaptive Diagnostics
frozenVsAdaptive.content: Suites V1–V3 represent a progressive benchmark culminating in the balanced 50-case frozen holdout (V3). Suites V4–V8 are iterative, adversarial diagnostic probes designed to expose failure modes, not stationary holdouts.
frozenVsAdaptive.rule: Results on V4–V8 describe targeted stress-test behavior, not generalized population accuracy.

repeatedRuns.title: Repeated Identical Evaluations
repeatedRuns.content: Running identical inputs across repeated trials (10 to 20 runs) characterizes empirical stochastic switching under fixed temperature and prompt states. These repeated trials quantify local volatility, not independent statistical samples.
repeatedRuns.rule: Choice frequencies (e.g. 14/6 in V5U02) are descriptive observations, not parametric probabilities.

confidenceSignal.title: Confidence Signal Limits
confidenceSignal.content: Raw confidence values reflect model probability mass assigned to the top candidate action. High confidence can co-occur with misclassifications on edge cases, while low confidence can produce correct routing.
confidenceSignal.rule: Confidence is a provider-returned uncertainty signal, not a calibrated probability of correctness.

marginSignal.title: Candidate Margin Separation
marginSignal.content: The decision-boundary margin is calculated strictly as margin = P(top1) - P(top2). Narrow margins indicate competition between adjacent actions, but do not provide an empirically validated universal threshold.
marginSignal.rule: Margin compression signals local competition, not a universal cutoff for production gating.

infrastructureDrops.title: Infrastructure Failures vs. Semantic Errors
infrastructureDrops.content: Operational dropped requests, HTTP timeouts, and upstream network drops are reported separately from semantic routing errors. In V4, V5, and Nemotron evaluations, operational drops were isolated from candidate discrimination.
infrastructureDrops.rule: Infrastructure reliability and semantic discrimination must not be conflated into a single score.

providerComparisons.title: Provider Comparison Limitations
providerComparisons.content: Jev, GPT-5-mini, and Nemotron Ultra were evaluated across differing cloud gateways, inference runtimes, and networking stacks. Comparisons are descriptive of observed runs under test conditions.
providerComparisons.rule: Cross-provider results do not establish a universal model ranking or permanent capability hierarchy.

costLatencyAccounting.title: Cost & Latency Comparability
costLatencyAccounting.content: Latency metrics included retry outliers in cloud gateways, and cost accounting differed across sources (observed gateway market pricing vs. theoretical list pricing vs. free experimental tiers).
costLatencyAccounting.rule: Observed market cost and latency reflect experimental testbed conditions, not production SLAs.

architectureStatus.title: Future Architecture & Governor Status
architectureStatus.content: The illustrated Uncertainty Governor schema represents an architectural concept separating routing uncertainty from deterministic permissions. It is not an empirical finding or a production-certified runtime component.
architectureStatus.rule: Routing uncertainty mitigation must remain distinct from deterministic security and safety controls.
